newsitem.title: UK: Country Casual sees upturn after poor year.
newsitem.headline: Country Casual sees upturn after poor year.

text.p: British clothing retailer Country Casuals Holdings Plc said on Thursday that it was encouraged by trading in recent months.
It said that each of its three businesses, Country Casual Ltd, Elvi and Lerose Manufacturing, has the potential for "considerable improvement over the coming year.

Country Casuals, which is in the process of restructuring the group, also reported that annual pretax profit slipped to 108,000 stg after losses at Elvi and Lerose from 249,000 previously. Group sales were little changed at 54.4 million.

The company announced earlier this week that it was in talks with its chief executive Mark Bunce that might lead to an offer for the group. It is also discussing the sale of Elvi and Lerose businesses with "potential purchasers".
Country Casuals is not paying a final dividend, making a total for the year of 1.70p from 5.41p.
